plain_text:
Smart Businesses Are Using Smart Paper Programs
Source: Natural Resources Defense Council, www.nrdc.org/cities/living/paper/companies.asp
Norm Thompson Outfitters
Catalog retailers mail out about 17 billion catalogs every year—that’s nearly 60 per person in the United States—and almost none of them use post-consumer recycled content paper. That’s why Norm Thompson’s cutting-edge, industry-leading commitment is so valuable. Norm Thompson prints its catalogs on 10% post-consumer recycled paper, and has set a company goal of increasing that figure to an average of 30% post-consumer recycled paper in the short term. The company estimates that it has saved:
• 4,400 tons of wood per year• 20 billion BTUs of energy
• 11.7 million gallons of water
• 990 tons of solid wasteBy being as efficient as possible and using their website to show the full breadth of products offered, they can also limit the number of pages they print.

plain_text:
Small Companies Do Make a BIG Difference
Source: Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, www.deq.state.or.us/tg/sw/cwrc/success/material/officepaper.htm
Bend Community School (Bend, Oregon)What They Do to Save Paper:
Number of Employees: 3Reduced paper use by encouraging double-sided copying, placing a bin next to the copy machine with “draft” paper (paper that is already used on one side, but can be reused), and turning off the automatic transmission report on the fax machine.
Hood River County Chamber of Commerce (Hood River, Oregon)What They Do to Save Paper:
Number of Employees: 7Began duplexing copies and using single-sided documents to print draft documents and for notepads. Since instituting these changes, paper consumption has been cut by nearly 40 percent.
